ga_glove_area.blurb: The Glove is a cluster of granite boulders inside the Boat Rock bouldering park in southwest Atlanta, set among houses and reached by a short walk in from the small lot. It holds 14 problems, nearly all of them between V2 and V4, with a handful of easy warm-ups and a few real stretches up to the V7 range and one problem at about V9. Expect low-angle slabs, balancy friction, an arete and some crack lines on abrasive crystalline rock that is hard on skin. A crash pad and spotter are worth bringing, and the sector suits a mixed group that wants moderate problems close together.

ga_indian_seats.blurb: Indian Seats is a small north-facing outcrop on Sawnee Mountain near Cumming, north of Atlanta, reached by hiking a trail to the summit area and then scrambling down below the overlook. Thirteen routes are mostly top-rope face climbs with fixed anchors, ranging from easy 5.5 and 5.6 up through a cluster of 5.7s and 5.8s, with a single 5.10 and one crack line that takes trad gear. The low grades and ready-made anchors make it a handy spot for beginners and for practising top-rope setups, and the north aspect keeps it on the cooler side.

ga_buzzard_wall_the.blurb: The Buzzard Wall is a mid-sized cliff on Currahee Mountain near Toccoa in northeast Georgia, lying beyond the gully at the far end of the slab section. Roughly a dozen lines mix trad and bolted sport routes, with anchors for top-roping on some. Grades start around 5.7 and run up to 5.13, but most of the routes sit in the 5.9 to 5.11 range, so it suits climbers who already lead the 5.10s. Newer development has gone in on the left side. Buzzards often circle overhead, which gave the wall its name.
